neighbours.label: an opening parenthesis that starts an aside in mid-sentence ( (but not always), (at least in print) )
fire: It often (but not always) includes a short training course.
This word is best (at least in print) written with an accent.
The library (on the fourth floor) is open to all members.
Our guide (a retired teacher) knew every street in the town.
The results were good (better than we expected) in every group.
He finally arrived (two hours late) with the keys.
Most of the cakes (especially the lemon ones) sold out quickly.
The old bridge (built in 1890) was closed for repairs.
